title: Random Forest selection guided discovery of nine TRAPUM millisecond pulsars
summary: A Random Forest classifier identified Fermi-LAT sources as pulsar candidates; the team observed 79 selected sources with MeerKAT and reported nine new millisecond pulsars, eight in binaries. The paper reports that all nine candidate signals were subsequently confirmed by additional detections. The authors separately note an independent redetection of one pulsar that had already been discovered elsewhere; it is not counted among the nine new MSPs. This is the 2022 preprint version of a 2023 MNRAS paper.
ai_technology: Random Forest classification of unassociated Fermi-LAT sources
organization: Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics (Albert Einstein Institute); Leibniz Universität Hannover; Jodrell Bank Centre for Astrophysics, The University of Manchester; Max-Planck-Institut für Radioastronomie; South African Radio Astronomy Observatory

evidence.tested: The source reports that a Random Forest classified 4FGL unassociated sources, 79 selected sources were observed with MeerKAT, and nine new MSPs were detected and subsequently confirmed by additional detections. Eight were in binary systems.
evidence.unknown: The paper describes nine discoveries as new and distinguishes a separate previously discovered pulsar redetected independently. This review did not conduct a separate external catalog audit of every pulsar designation.
evidence.ai_role: A Random Forest classified unassociated 4FGL sources to choose pulsar candidates for the targeted MeerKAT survey in which the nine new MSPs were discovered.
